main_strengths: The Monetarist reasoning is genuine, not decoration. 15/17 trajectories run the money-growth vs real-growth-plus-target test on the actual numbers (the other two state it). They treat supply shocks as relative-price changes that become inflation only if money accommodates them, and use velocity (9/17), rules vs discretion and long and variable lags (6/17). No Keynesian or Austrian vocabulary appears in any trajectory.

Several trajectories use the school's own tool for the event: sterilized vs unsterilized FX intervention (m0005), money multiplier vs high-powered money for an RRR cut (m0018), stablecoins as private money and a velocity shock (m0010), tariffs as a one-time price-level change with Smoot-Hawley under contracting money (m0019), and credit vs money in mortgage relief (m0017).

Most signal directions follow the event and backdrop rather than a default. Easing and support events (m0000, m0005, m0007, m0017, m0018) get risk-on sets. High-M2 backdrops flip bonds to SHORT (m0011, m0012, m0014, m0019), and an event that states above-target inflation does too (m0002). Oil goes LONG for supply shocks, SHORT for demand shocks and NEUTRAL when the chain doesn't touch it (m0009, m0014). Bonds are balanced at 7 LONG, 7 SHORT, 3 NEUTRAL.

Every analog is real and dated before 2025, and most are apt (2001/2008/2020 intermeeting cuts, the 1998/2000/2011 US FX interventions, Terra, Reserve Primary and USDC, HAMP, PBoC RRR cuts in 2008/2015/2018). The macro observations copy the backdrop exactly in 17/17 (one has a malformed key). Probabilities sum to 1 and every signal has a conviction and a reason.
main_problems: Wrong money-growth benchmark: M2 is compared with one quarter's q/q saar GDP (-4 to +5 here), never with trend real growth (0/17). The verdict therefore swings on noise and is applied inconsistently: 3.5% against -1.0% is called non-accommodative (m0001), but 4.8% against -0.5% is called excessive (m0002). The quantity equation is never written out, and only m0017 (implicitly m0007) infers velocity from the data.

One stock mechanism dominates. 'Relative-price shock, inflation only if money accommodates' appears in 15/17, up to 10 times per trajectory, including for demand and financial shocks (PMI, unemployment, EM default, shutdown). The natural rate of unemployment appears 0/17 times, even for the unemployment event (m0011). The quantity theory, real balances and Friedman-Schwartz are never named.

Spurious event-vs-backdrop 'conflict' sentences in 8/17 (m0000, m0003, m0005, m0009, m0010, m0015, m0016, m0017): prompt rule 4 gets applied to every new shock that would move a pre-event variable. m0005 reverses the logic. Only m0002 has a real contradiction.

Templated scenarios and probabilities. S1 is always the modal scenario at 0.45-0.55, and the split 0.55/0.25/0.20 appears in 8/17 (7 in that exact order). Signal reasons almost never weigh other scenarios: 97 of 102 lines cite S1, 4 cite a chain step and 1 adds S3 (prompt: 'signals follow the most likely scenario'). That ignores 45-55% of the probability mass. Some S1 labels run backwards: easing leads to 'inflation down' (m0000, m0018) and stable money to 'inflation up' (m0017). In 10/17, two scenarios carry the same growth/inflation directions, so the labels cannot separate temporary from persistent inflation.

The teacher writes the tool outputs. get_macro_data comes back in 4 formats and query_episode_db in 12 different layouts or key sets, with one malformed key (m0014). 6/17 drop the Scenarios:/Signals: headers. Every item runs the identical two-call script and requests all 13 indicators. A student trained on this learns to make up tool results and a fixed call order.
Boilerplate: 13/17 first [Think] blocks state that the event gives no size in bp, pp or share of GDP (rule 1), even for a PMI level or a stated 200% freight jump.

Some analogs misstate money growth: 1998, when M2 accelerated and inflation was below target (m0002); the 2012 drought, during QE3 with M2 near 7% (m0009); euro M3 in 2019 (m0001); Argentina 2008, which was over export taxes (m0019); and a garbled Argentina 2001 currency-board lesson (m0016).

Default-looking directions: gold is never SHORT (8 LONG, 9 NEUTRAL), even with tight money and a firmer dollar. The dollar is NEUTRAL in 9/17. A minor foreign shutdown gets the full risk-off set (m0015).

Input problems the teacher accepts without comment. The backdrop generator produces implausible mixes (10y at 0.3% with 7.2% CPI; a 5.5% policy rate with -0.2% core PCE; 0.3% CPI with $126 oil). It has no lagged money or trend-growth series, so 'long and variable lags' can be asserted but never shown. Templates leave size and commodity unclear ('500bn' with no currency or period; 'major commodity producer' and 'major shipping strait' unnamed), and the teacher fills the gap with oil LONG 4.
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: School diagnosis (templates.toml, monetarist): 'Compare M2 growth with trend real growth (about 2.5-3%) plus the 2% target, i.e. about 4.5-5%; one quarter's q/q saar GDP is noise. Where it helps, back out implied velocity growth (CPI + real GDP - M2). Separate supply shocks (relative prices) from money-demand, velocity and credit shocks; do not call a demand or financial shock a relative-price shock.'

Make the mechanism event-dependent with a per-category hint. Labour and data releases: natural rate and expectations-augmented Phillips curve. Balance-sheet, RRR and FX events: monetary base vs broad money, multiplier, sterilization. Fiscal events: fiscal changes move nominal spending only if money moves. Financial crises: money demand and velocity, and whether the central bank prevents a broad-money contraction.
Rule 1: replace the size clause with 'If the event states a size, use it to judge materiality; if not, do not comment on missing units.' Validator: reject the 'bp, pp, or share of GDP' disclaimer.

Rule 4: 'Mention a contradiction only when the event states a level the backdrop contradicts (e.g. inflation 2pp above target vs CPI 1.4%). A shock that would move a variable away from its pre-event value is not a contradiction.' Better still, condition the backdrop on levels the event states (T01-05) so there is nothing to contradict.

Rule 5: replace 'The signals follow the most likely scenario' with 'Signals reflect the probability-weighted scenarios; if S1 is below 0.6 and another scenario points the other way, cut conviction or go NEUTRAL; reasons may cite several scenarios.' Add 'Scenarios must differ in growth or inflation direction; labels must follow from the mechanism; probabilities come from this event and backdrop, not a 0.55/0.25/0.20 default; for a foreign event say whose growth and inflation.' Have collect() report the distribution of S1 probabilities and repeated probability tuples, as it already does for direction shares.

Stop letting the teacher write [Observe]. Render get_macro_data from the backdrop in one canonical JSON format, and back query_episode_db with a curated, fact-checked episode table in one schema. Generate in two stages (teacher writes up to the tool call, the harness injects the result, the teacher continues), or at least mask [Observe] tokens from the SFT loss. Allow subsets of indicators and a data-first order for data-release events.

macro_snapshot: tie the 10y and policy rate to inflation and unemployment (Fisher/Taylor with noise), let oil co-move with CPI, and add 'M2 growth y/y, 12 months earlier', 'nominal GDP growth y/y' and 'real GDP growth, 4-quarter average'. That lets velocity and lags be computed from data instead of asserted. Fewer impossible regimes also stop the student learning spurious relations.

Templates: render T01-04 as '$500bn over 12 months' (or per month); use the existing commodity slot in T05-04 and name the strait or its cargo in T05-02; rephrase T02-06 for economies without shutdown mechanisms (e.g. a spending freeze under a provisional budget).

Asset menu: tell the teacher gold can be SHORT under tight money, rising real rates and a firmer dollar, and add a warning to the batch report when an asset's direction count is 0 (gold SHORT 0/17). For events about grain, freight or copper, allow NEUTRAL with conviction 1 rather than proxying through oil.
Before scaling: keep m0012, m0014, m0010, m0007, m0019 and m0016 as exemplars. Regenerate m0015, m0000, m0018 and m0005 (backwards scenario labels or reversed logic), and fix m0002's 1998 analog.
